headline: Billionaire and big-business Shorts reach 8–12 times more people than personal-budget ones; the first 6 seconds after the hook lose the most viewers.

working.text: Shorts with a dollar figure or 'billion' in the title: median 793 views in 48 h (9 videos) vs 39 for the rest (24).
Shorts under 40 s: median 49.0% viewed and 128 views in 48 h (16), vs 34.3% and 46 views for 40 s+ (18).
'Secret' hooks: median 708 views in 48 h and 43.8% viewed (5 videos).

notWorking.text: 'Myth' hooks: median 12 views in 48 h and 23.5% viewed (5 videos).
Announcing the structure ('four levels', 'three clues') right after the hook lost 24–41% of viewers in 2 s in five recent Shorts.
Long videos: 3 published, median 1 view in 48 h and 0.6% viewed.

audience.text: 28 days: India 35%, US 12.5%, Philippines 12.3%, Indonesia 8.7%, UK 6.3% of views.
Mostly men: 25–34 male 32%, 35–44 male 16%, 18–24 male 15%; 35–44 female 11%.
99.4% of views are from non-subscribers; 13 net subscribers in 28 days on 11,105 views.

recommendations.do: Keep at least 2 of every 3 Shorts about billionaires, famous companies and money at scale, with the dollar figure in the title.
recommendations.because: Those Shorts got a median 793 views in 48 h vs 39 for the rest.

recommendations.do: After the hook, never announce the structure ('four levels', 'three clues'); show the first answer as a picture by 5 s.
recommendations.because: Those lines lost 24–41% of viewers in about 2 seconds (e.g. 1.00 → 0.59 at 5.2 s on the $1 salary Short).

recommendations.do: End each Short with a reason to follow (a series promise) since almost no viewer is a subscriber.
recommendations.because: 99.4% of views are from non-subscribers and only 13 subscribers came from 11,105 views.
